categories.name: Organic Waste
categories.label: Green
categories.desc: Waste that naturally biodegrades in the environment.
categories.guide: Never dispose of in plastic bags. Use dedicated composting bins or local organic waste collection.
categories.examples: Food scraps, spoiled vegetables, tea bags, coffee grounds, leaves, eggshells.
categories.impact: Composting organic waste reduces methane emissions from landfills and creates nutrient-rich natural fertilizer for soil.

categories.name: Recyclables
categories.label: Blue
categories.desc: Clean and dry materials that can be processed into new products.
categories.guide: Ensure items are completely empty, clean, and dry before sorting. Flatten boxes to save space.
categories.examples: Clean paper, cardboard boxes, aluminum cans, glass bottles, clean food containers.
categories.impact: Recycling these materials conserves natural resources, reduces energy consumption, and prevents valuable materials from ending up in landfills.

categories.name: Plastic Waste
categories.label: Yellow
categories.desc: Various types of plastics (PET, HDPE, etc.) that require specific recycling processes.
categories.guide: Empty all liquids, crush bottles to save space, and remove caps/labels if required by your local facility.
categories.examples: Water bottles (PET), milk jugs (HDPE), shampoo bottles, plastic food trays, clean plastic bags.
categories.impact: Proper plastic recycling prevents microplastic pollution in our oceans and reduces the need for virgin fossil fuel extraction.

categories.name: Hazardous Waste
categories.label: Red
categories.desc: Materials containing toxic, reactive, or flammable chemicals.
categories.guide: NEVER mix with regular trash. Store safely and drop off at designated e-waste or hazardous material collection points.
categories.examples: Batteries, old electronics, fluorescent bulbs, paint, motor oil, chemical cleaning agents.
categories.impact: Correct disposal prevents toxic heavy metals and chemicals from leaching into groundwater and contaminating the ecosystem.

categories.name: Other Waste
categories.label: Gray
categories.desc: Non-recyclable and non-organic household waste destined for landfill or incineration.
categories.guide: This waste goes directly to landfills. Try your best to minimize this category through mindful purchasing.
categories.examples: Styrofoam, heavily soiled pizza boxes, broken ceramics, diapers, used tissues.
categories.impact: Reducing this waste category directly extends the lifespan of landfills and minimizes the environmental footprint of waste incineration.
